text:
Zoe (Marketing): quick launch ask — need a reproducible 10k stratified rerun for the press deck + webinar. Focus: tail latency and multilingual failure modes. Buckets: <32, 32-256, 256-1024, >1024. Langs: en, es, zh, ar, other. Run both rwd-7b-v1 (fp32) and rwd-7b-q4_0_v2. Deliverables: per-slice p50/p90/p99, token-cost, failure rate, and raw traces. Please include prompt-length CDF and seeds. Target by Mon EOD?

Jordan (Runtime): can do. clarifications: 1) warm vs cold separation? 2) routing mix: prod proportions vs equal per-lang? 3) concurrency sweep?

Zoe (Marketing): separate warm/cold. define warm = warmup_tokens=3 and tag with header X-Bench-Warm=1. Use production routing mix but ensure min 1k samples per language. Include concurrency sweep 4/8/16. Use seed=9999 for reproducibility. Cap extreme sequences at 8192.

Maya (Eng): heads-up: >1024 hits different kernel path, expect skewed p99 and token-cost. recommend logging kernel_path and kernel_fallback_count. If zh failures concentrate, try zh warmup=8 in follow-up.

Sam (Ops): scheduling low-priority run on staging at 02:00 UTC tomorrow. example commands i'll run: 

```
./run_bench --model=rwd-7b-v1 --quant=fp32 --samples=10000 --seed=9999 \\n  --buckets="<32,32-256,256-1024,>1024" --langs="en,es,zh,ar,other" \\n  --min_per_lang=1000 --warmup_tokens=3 --warm_header="X-Bench-Warm=1" \\n  --concurrency=8 --batch=32 --cap=8192 --tag=marketing-launch

./run_bench --model=rwd-7b-q4_0_v2 --quant=q4_0 --same-flags
```

benchbot: job queued -> jb-20260309-900. ETA ~5h. logs: https://ci/internal/jb-20260309-900/logs

benchbot: jb-20260309-900 completed. artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/marketing/5187654321/. quick first-pass: q4_0_v2 shows better p50 on <32 tokens but ~11% p99 regression on >1024. overall failure rate 0.31%, concentrated on long zh samples. kernel_fallback_count: 28 (mostly zh). per-slice CSVs and raw traces in bucket.

Zoe (Marketing): great — this is exactly the data we need. we'll review and request a zh-focused warmup run if required. thanks! :tada:
